terminology_notes: Main inconsistencies: (1) 'Giftable spares' has two renderings and one of them ('rezervne kopije') means 'backups'; (2) 'Redeem' split between 'unovčiti' and 'uveljaviti', the latter also used for 'Claim'; (3) 'Refresh' split between 'Osveži' and 'Posodobi'; (4) 'native' split between 'nativno' and 'izvorno'; (5) 'Steam knjižnica' vs 'knjižnica Steam' word order varies (both acceptable; 'knjižnica Steam' is more standard); (6) brand inflection: accusative 'v Steam' is correct, but locative/instrumental 'na Steam'/'s Steam' should be 'v Steamu'/'s Steamom'; 'na Humblovi' shows the translator can inflect, so the bare forms are inconsistency, not policy; (7) typography: ellipsis sometimes spaced ('…' vs ' …') and ASCII straight quotes used where Slovenian uses „…“ — not flagged per row; (8) 'bottle' left in English with inconsistent agreement; (9) 'Redeem a Steam key' is 'Unovčite' (formal imperative) in the dialog title but 'Unovči' in the sidebar.
overall:
The Slovenian translation is generally competent: meaning is preserved in nearly all rows, all {{placeholders}}, the <3> tag,
and " entities are intact, and no row inverts or loses a critical meaning. The notable problems are terminology — 'Giftable spares' rendered as 'rezervne kopije' (backups) with a second, different rendering in the irreversible-action warning, and 'Redeem' vs 'Claim' collapsing onto 'uveljaviti' in the Humble Keys flow — plus systematic uninflected brand locatives ('na Steam') and missing Slovenian dual/paucal plural forms. I am confident on the grammar and terminology calls; stylistic calls (question phrasing, theme names) are judgement, and without rendered UI context I did not flag gender agreements that depend on the runtime placeholder value (e.g. '{{packageName}} je bil dodan').
